questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot. Going by his Blundstone videos, he says most pretreated Blundstones shouldn't be treated out of the box, but distressed or rustic leathers (like his rustic brown pair) are worth conditioning. As for how often, in 2022 he said there's no fixed schedule: treat them when they look or feel dry.

**Out of the box**
- In 2019 he read Blundstone's FAQ: most Blundstones are pretreated, so Blundstone doesn't recommend treating them out of the box, and he notes that if you try, products just roll off. [1]
- The exception is rustic brown, Crazy Horse brown or rustic black leathers. Those are distressed and don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather. [2]
- He recommends conditioning those rustic boots, and he says he wouldn't recommend keeping them dry. His reason is that dry leather cracks and gets brittle. [3] Expect oil to darken them. [2]
- In his first review he first thought his distressed pair was already water resistant, then took that back. He later corrected the review, saying the FAQ shows rustic leathers aren't pretreated like finished leathers. [4][5]
- Even in that first review, he recommended the boots only if you'll keep them treated. Otherwise he suggested plastic or Gore-Tex boots. [6]

**How often**
- His latest word (2022) is that he isn't sure and expects flak either way. He personally probably treats too little, and does it when he feels they need it. [7]
- He says how often depends on how much you wear them and where you go. [7]
- Signs they need treatment: they look or feel dry, or water isn't beading on top. Wax helps with beading, and oil helps if they look dry. He also says to clean them regularly, since dirt wears leather down faster. [7]
- In 2019 he said you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week if you're really hard on them, and brush off salt. [6]

**His order of steps (2022):** clean, condition, then wax. [8]

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, they shrink the first time you soak or wash them, but he says that's why you size up, and with the right sizing they end up fitting normally. His most recent view (2025) is that you should usually go two sizes up in the waist, since they're sanforized-free denim that shrinks.

**Newest take (2025):** He says the Levi's 501 STF is unsanforized denim, so you put it in the bathtub and it shrinks. He says you should usually go two sizes up. [1]

**How the sizing works (2021, 2023):** He says Levi's recommends going two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer. He first ignored this, but after going through several pairs he concluded Levi's is correct. If you follow it, the pants fit regularly after you get them wet. [2] In the 2023 Wrangler comparison, his size 32 STFs were a true 16.5-inch-across waist, which is why you size up two. That is also why he expected shrunk STFs to end up smaller than rinsed 501s in size 30. [3]

**How tight they get:**
- In 2019 he sized only slightly up and the waist was very tight after shrinking. He described it as feeling like someone punching him in the stomach, but he said it isn't that constricting. [4] After a week of wear, the waist and upper thigh had stretched enough that he could wear a belt. [5]
- Length barely changed for him. [6]

**Washing matters:** In 2023 he said the shrunk STFs looked way better because he didn't use very hot water or the dryer. His advice is not to toss STFs in the dryer or rinse them that hot, and you can get a really nice fit. [7]

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
By his rule, you'd buy a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF. He hasn't talked about Levi's 502s, so this applies his general advice to your 502 size.

**His rule (most recent first):** In 2025 he says you should usually go two sizes up in the STF 501 [1]. In 2021 he says Levi's own advice is right: size up two in the waist and two inches longer in length. He admits it took him four pairs of 501s to learn this [2]. By his rule, a 33 waist becomes 35 and a 30 length becomes 32.

**Waist:** In 2023 he notes that the STF waist doesn't follow vanity sizing, which is why he sizes up two [3]. In 2021 he also says a 34 would become a 36, "although i don't think a 36 exists" [2]. He hasn't said whether a 35 is available, so check that before you order.

**Length:** In 2020 he says he "definitely would have gotten a 32" after buying a 30 length. He cuffed them anyway [4].

**His own experiment:** In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a 29x30 because jeans are usually too long on him [5]. A year later he said he could barely pull them on at first, but the waist now fits well. He still wished he had gone with a 32 length [4]. In 2021 he said he had messed up by not following Levi's advice [2].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
His most recent explanation (2020) is that cuffing suits his current style, which doesn't lend itself to uncuffed wider-legged pants. He also says he'd have bought the 501s in a 32 length, but he cuffed them anyway [1].

**Style (2020):** He says he cuffed his Levi's 501s "just because i don't think my current style kind of lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants" [1].

**Length and proportion (2019):** In his first 501 video, he says length matters most to him: if jeans look too long, they "just look bad," and that's "the first and foremost thing." A basic cuff made the wide, unshrunk 501s fit and feel a little better. He also says the cuff can't be too thick [2]. He tried a pin roll too, which looked a little better, though the legs were still wider than he likes [2].

**With boots (late 2019):** With boots, he says he used to always cuff his jeans, but now he likes them down over the boots a bit more. He thinks that calms the boots down as a loud fashion statement [3].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, he has preferred the 3335s over the 1907s, but his latest word (September 2023) is hedged: he's selling them, and says they "still might be" his favorite Red Wings, "but they probably not" the 875s, 1907s or Iron Rangers.

**Latest view (2023):** He says he's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time, and that this still might be true, but they probably aren't the best, since the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1]. He still likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight, and nimbler feel, and says they're easier for walking or a light hike. But they're going from his collection [1].

**Earlier view (October 2022):** He called the 3335s his favorite boots he's ever had, saying they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [2]. His reasons:
- He's not doing heritage work, but going for hikes and walking in the woods, so for him they're a dramatically better all-around boot [2].
- He prefers the Vibram mini lug sole, a very heavy dense rubber he doesn't think will break down as fast as the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [3].
- He finds them cooler-looking [4].

**Caveats:** The 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot, he says the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [2]. He also says the 3335s' stitch-down construction isn't a big edge over a Goodyear-welted boot like the 1907 here, because they use a single stitch [5]. The 3335s run true to size, but their slim, tapered profile squeezed his toes with wool socks [6].

**Earlier on the 1907 (2021):** He called the 1907 the best Red Wing moc toe, arguing it costs about $10 more than the 875 but adds a storm welt, a removable leather footbed and leather laces [7].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, The Iron Snail is still a big Blundstone fan, even though he is retiring his own pair. He says "Bluntstones are just incredible I'm a big fan of them I've always loved them" [1]. He adds that some people seem to really not like them [1].

**His 585s (2023):** These are the pair from his first ever video, and they hold a special place in his heart [2]. He has worn them constantly, and the leather is beat up and shiny with old wax and conditioner. They have held up through all of it and remain probably his most water resistant boots [1]. He still says "I think it's time to retire those bunnies" [1]. He frames the cull as clearing out his collection [3].

**The heavy-duty Extremes (2023):** He is also letting go of the Blundstone 989 Extreme Series. He had thought they were waterproof, but they are only very water-resistant nubuck [4].

**Earlier view (2019):** In his first-impressions review he recommended them "100%" if you will keep them treated. He called them by far his favorites of the three or four boots he had [5][6]. His main gripe was that the soles can't officially be replaced [7].

So his 2023 view is not a change of heart on the boots. He still rates them highly and is selling his pairs to make room.

questions.question: I'm wondering if you still have these boots and how are they holding up??? [Blundstones]

hybrid.answer:
Yes, as of his most recent word (September 2023) he still had his Blundstone 585s, but he was retiring them. He says they've held up well and are still his most water resistant boots.

**Latest (Sept 2023):** He describes wearing them constantly since he got them. The leather is "all beat up" and "super shiny" with old wax conditioner on it, yet they've "held up through it all" and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [1]. He's a big fan, but says "it's time to retire those bunnies" [1]. He lists them as a pair that he's letting go in the boot cull [2]. He also says Blundstones are shoes he can flop on quickly regardless of weather, and he keeps a slip-on pair for that, though he says it could easily go on the sell list [3].

**June 2022 (about two years in):** He wore them from when it gets cold until mid-spring, and the rustic brown leather had become quite worn [4]. He restored them by cleaning, conditioning with salve and oil, and waxing for water resistance [5].

**August 2020 (one year):** They looked great after a year. Elastics were slightly looser but still tight, and the scuffs from mountain descents were more than he expected, with lining wear at the big toe [6]. He'd have chosen a smoother leather than the rustic nubuck, which shows wear more [7]. He hadn't treated them for that year, yet they stayed dry in a pond test, apart from the elastic band getting a little wet [8].

He hasn't said what happens to them after the 2023 video.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He prefers Solovair over the Made in England Dr. Martens for most buyers. He says it's the cheaper, better-built boot, and the main reason to pay more for Made in England is that you're a big Dr. Martens fan.

**Newest view (2023).** In his Made in England vs. Thailand video he doesn't mention Solovair. He does say the England boots are probably not worth the extra $90 on a purely practical basis [1]. He adds that right now you have to be a mega fan to get them [2]. That fits his earlier Solovair recommendation.

**Where Made in England and Solovair are equal (2022).** He says the Made in England leather will age fine and is probably on par with Solovair, and the midsoles are probably also on par [3].

**Why he favors Solovair (2022).**
- **Price:** Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Docs [4]. He says most of the roughly third added to the price is the "made in England" part itself [5].
- **Comfort:** Solovair boots have a shank, so they're more comfortable over long periods [6]. Docs have no shank, which he says makes them easier to break in but more tiring over time [7]. Solovairs are a bit tougher to break in but give you more comfort down the line [8].
- **Resoling:** Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [9].
- **Same boot:** The derby eight-eyed Solovair is essentially the exact same boot as the Dr. Martens, from the original maker. The only thing it lacks is the yellow stitching [10].

**Caveat.** His own Solovairs had problems after eight wears: a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He believes it was a manufacturing defect and expected the company to fix it [11].

**Bottom line.** If you want the highest-quality Doc Martens and the yellow stitching matters, he says you have to get Made in England. If not, he suggests going to Solovair [10].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He hasn't covered multi-day hiking in Blundstones, but what he has said suggests they're a weak pick for a 4-day hike, mainly because of the lack of ankle support.

**Ankle support (his main caution).** In his 2020 one-year review he says he took his Blundstones up and down mountains in Maine and they "held up well" [1]. He also says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [2]. He doesn't say how they'd do over several days in a row.

**Break-in.** Brand-new, he had no blisters on a day of walking in 2019 [3]. In 2020, though, he got "big fat gross blisters like break-in blisters for boots" when he started running and walking the track in them. These stopped after about two to three weeks [4]. If yours aren't already well broken in, that's worth knowing before a long trek.

**Water.** In 2023 he calls his worn pair "probably my most water resistant boots through it all" [5]. His advice is that the water resistance only lasts if you keep the boots treated [6]. He also says they can handle a brook or stream crossing or standing in mud, but he wouldn't stand in still water in them [7].

**What he hasn't covered:** pack weight, multi-day comfort, and blister risk over consecutive days. His opinions here come from day hikes and everyday wear, not a multi-day trip.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** The Iron Snail's pick for cost and quality is the Uniqlo crew neck, but for someone taller or wider than average he says to get the Muji instead. He hasn't given a size for your height and weight, so the sizing part is only partly covered.

**Best value for you: Muji (or Uniqlo)**
- In his September 2025 roundup he says the $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [1]
- He then adds that if you're taller or wider, you'd want the Muji. It costs about $4 or $5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider. [2]
- In June 2025 he said Uniqlo's price-to-quality ratio is insane, with a bound neck collar so it doesn't wiggle. [3] He also said the Muji feels justified at roughly $10 more because it feels better. [4]
- At 5'11" and 225 lb, his advice applied to you points to the Muji first, with the Uniqlo as the cheaper fallback.

**Other options**
- **Cheaper:** In 2024 he said he can't recommend the Kirkland six-pack enough if you want a shirt under $5 or $6. It shrank 4% in width and 2% in length. [5]
- **A step up:** He calls the $35 House of Blanks (combed ringspun, made in Canada) an outstanding value. [6]

**Size**
- He doesn't give a size for your build.
- On fit, he says he likes a lot of space across the shoulders [7] and likes shirts that flatten him out. [8]
- His only explicit size tip is for Los Angeles Apparel: he thinks it might win if you size down one. [9]
- He also says the best shirt has to line up with your own preferences. [10]

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
He deliberately doesn't name one winner, so you're not alone. In his latest roundup (Sept 2025) he says the best tee "just has to line up with your preferences" [1]. He does give a personal pick in each category, and those are the closest thing to "buy this."

**His personal winners (Sept 2025):**
- **All-arounder:** J. Press x American Trench, mainly because he likes its rougher hand feel [2].
- **Japanese:** Wonder Looper, over Samurai, for a better and more universal fit [3].
- **Heavyweight:** American Giant, "by a long shot," because it's a little lighter and fits more universally [3].
- **Elevated and minimal:** Merz b. Schwanen 2M15. He says Lady White could be his favorite, but on the day he felt MSB "eekes out just a little bit" [4].
- **Budget:** Front General Store for character, or House of Blanks for perfectly smooth with no torque. He says "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" and might choose the other tomorrow [5].

**If you want one cheap, safe buy:** he says the $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [6].

**Older and other views:**
- In 2023 his favorite by far was the roughly $100 Standard & Strange Wakayama Special [7].
- In 2024 he named Asket the overall winner among shirts he paid for [8].
- He notes Bronson usually wins or comes close in other people's comparisons [9]. He left it out of his Sept 2025 list.

**How to narrow it down using his advice:** choose by price and feel. For $20 to $40, go Uniqlo or Front General Store. For a premium, flowy, clean look, go MSB or Lady White. For something extremely heavy, go American Giant. He hasn't said "buy these 3," so that final call is yours.

questions.question: Do you have any particular favorites for more athletic builds? I sometimes have trouble with high quality tees being tight on the shoulders and boxy around the waist

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail doesn't single out a tee for athletic builds in the videos available here, so nothing below is a direct athletic-fit recommendation. A few of his fit comments are still relevant to your two problems.

**Tight shoulders**
- He likes the J.Press x American Trench tee for its room: he calls it a "good freaking fit" and says he likes a lot of space [1] across the shoulders [2]. It's in his "all-arounders" group, which he'd recommend to anybody [1]. This is the closest he comes to your shoulder complaint.
- He picked it as his favorite in that category, partly for its rougher hand feel [3].

**Boxy vs. flowing fits**
- The closest he gets to athletic builds is Asket. He says it's what he imagines "very jacked or slim men wearing at coffee shops because it just flows, feels like glass" [4]. That's his impression rather than a fit test. Asket also didn't make his final list because that list was for tees under $50 [4].
- Merz b. Schwanen was his pick in the Supremes category. He likes its unique fit, especially across the neck and chest [5].
- Wonder Looper is his pick among the Japanese tees because it has "a much better fit, much more universal fit" [6]. Samurai, by contrast, is cropped and wide, so you might not like it [6].

**Not covered:** he doesn't say how any of these taper through the waist, so he hasn't addressed boxiness as such. Muji is the one he suggests for bigger guys, since it's longer and wider, which probably works against a less boxy fit [7].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** He prefers the 1907 over the 875 (2021), mostly for the storm welt and the extras you get for about $10 more. By 2023 he hedged: he says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes, and he doesn't name a winner between them.

**His latest view (2023):** The 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics that I really really like" [1]. In 2022 he said his favorite boot overall was the Red Wing 3335, which "beat the 1907s, they beat the 875s" [2]. He added that the 1907s and 875s are "more beefily constructed", so they suit someone who needs a tough boot [3].

**Construction**
- **875:** It is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "incredible" [4]. He says the welt leaves room for cork that molds to your foot over time [5].
- **1907:** It has a storm welt, which he calls "invaluable" [6]. He says the popular view (which he has seen on Reddit) is that Red Wing just stitches "another strip of leather onto the welt itself", and he isn't quite sure [7].

**Price and extras (2021):** He says the 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [8]. For that, it comes with Red Wing's inner leather footbed, which he says is typically about $40 separately. It also comes with leather laces [6]. He says the footbeds can be pulled out to help the boots dry [6].

**Soles:** He says both the 875 and 1907 have crepe soles. He doesn't like them and thinks they break down faster than the Vibram sole on the 3335 [9].

**Waterproofing:** In his test, the right 1907 leaked almost immediately through the stitching [10]. He still has no doubt the boots would hold up in rain, grass or mud [10]. He didn't test the 875 the same way.

**His pick (2021):** If you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing, he says "i think you should get the 1907's" [11].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** Uniqlo is the one he keeps naming as the best budget t-shirt. Front General Store is a step up in price that he also rates very highly. Pro Club and Hanes only came up in his 2024 roundup, so he hasn't compared them to Uniqlo recently.

**Uniqlo (his budget pick)**
In September 2025 he said the $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He calls it your "starter t-shirt", open-ended and a bit rough. If you're taller or wider, he'd point you to Muji instead [2]. In June 2025 he praised the $15 version for its bound neck collar that "doesn't wiggle a lot" [3]. Back in 2024 he said that if you want a heavyweight, coarse-feeling tee with a bound, ribbed collar, "this may be" the best bargain [4].

**Front General Store**
In 2025 he called the $40 Japan-made tee a "previous winner" that "maybe" came second, with "great proportions, great feel" [5]. In June 2025 he still called it a "really good t-shirt" at around $38 [6]. In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want a Japanese-made upgrade without spending over $40. He gave it softness 6/10, and it was pre-washed so it barely shrank [7].

**Pro Club**
He said he understood why people are passionate about it. It was the roughest shirt on that list, but he liked everything about it [8]. He gave it softness 4/10 and a shrink of 2.78% in width and 6.86% in length [9].

**Hanes**
He called it "your classic $10 great shirt" with softness 7/10 and shrink of 1.45% in width and 6.73% in length [10]. He said it was much softer than Pro Club [11].

**Bottom line:** For value he points to Uniqlo ($15–$20). If you can spend about $40 for a Japan-made shirt, he likes Front General Store. In 2024 he was fine with Pro Club and Hanes, but they weren't his budget picks. In June 2025 he also said Bronson and Bravestar are neck and neck for value and "slightly above Uniclo" [12].

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
Going by his reasoning, he leans toward the Barbour for that mix of rain, wind and light spring wear. I'm assuming "this" means the Barbour, since you didn't say which jacket. He hasn't compared the two directly for wind or rain, so this is his stated points applied to your use.

**Barbour (his 2025 ranking, his top pick)**
- He says the Barbour is "not a designated rain jacket," and that it's the lightest-weight fabric in the lineup, 6 oz Sylkoil [1]. He says that flexibility means you can wear it in any season, including spring [2].
- It has storm cuffs, which he calls helpful in inclement weather [3]. It also comes with a hood and has snaps for it [3].
- In his 2021 review, a freshly waxed Bedale didn't leak in a shower test. He says Barbours aren't waterproof but are very water resistant when properly treated [4].
- The catch is that the wax wears off as the jacket develops patina, so it becomes less water resistant [5]. For rain use you'd need to keep up the wax.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
- He calls it a jacket for everyone: lighter weight but "not crazy lightweight" [6]. It's lined, so the wax doesn't touch your skin [7].
- His main selling point is the $300 price for a lined, US-made jacket in Martexin fabric [7].
- He doesn't say how it handles rain or wind, and the available videos don't mention a hood. Note that his Flint and Tinder segment was sponsored by Huckberry. He says he'd praised the jacket before the sponsorship [8].

**Bottom line**
For a rain-first, all-season, light layer, his Barbour comments fit your use better. He says the Barbour is the lightest of the group, and it comes with a hood and storm cuffs. The Flint and Tinder is a good-value everyday jacket, but he hasn't said it's suited to rain or wind.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
His con was about the specific Huckberry jacket he reviewed, which has no lining. He hasn't addressed the lined wool or flannel versions in the videos available here.

**What the con was (2023):** He called the Huckberry waxed trucker "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1]. His con was that the Huckberry and Rogue Territory jackets "are not lined." He says he personally always likes a lining on waxed jackets "just so the wax isn't touching your clothes or your arms or something like that" [2]. It's a personal preference, and he adds "other than that Flawless" [2]. So a lined version would fit his stated preference. He doesn't say whether he'd rate those versions differently.

**His later view (2025):** He has softened on lining. He says he "usually... always want[s] a liner, especially with wax jackets because it's waxy, so it gets on your skin" [3]. But "in my old age," he sees why you wouldn't line something. A satin sleeve lining "really limit[s] how often you can wear the jacket," because once it's a little warm it starts to stick to your skin [4]. He said this while discussing the Rogue Territory jacket, not the Huckberry one.

In short, the unlined con was always a matter of his taste, and by 2025 he was less firm about it.
